audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 3 and 4 read Skill while their own whys[] strings say 'You favour L1', 'You favour 4-5' and 'Sylas favours L6'.
audit.why: Packet chart is Tryndamere, Skill, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Sylas, Tryndamere, Tryndamere over 3059 games. The mirror moved the same five rows onto the packet read.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 3 to Tryndamere, row 4 to Sylas, as matched full/content pairs with ratings and reasons.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is described as 'his one good window' with a 'long R cooldown' to wait out. Hijack's cooldown is short, not long, and shorter than yours.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30 against Undying Rage at 120/100/80. At every rank he gets your ultimate back sooner than you do, so 'wait out his long R' is backwards advice. Kingslayer is 12/10.5/9/7.5/6 and heals off champions; Abscond is 13/12/11/10/9 against Spinning Slash at 12/11/10/9/8 — yours is exactly one second shorter at every rank, so you always own the last dash.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, spikes[1], whys[4], phases[4].why and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Abscond / Abduct is described as 'his dash + stun (recast pull)' in four places. It has no stun, and the recast pulls Sylas to the target rather than the target to Sylas.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' Nothing about a stun. Treating it as a stun makes players hold Flash for CC that does not exist, and treating it as a pull-in makes them stand at range they think is safe.
audit.corrected: Restated as a dash whose recast drags him to you, with the one-second cooldown edge over Spinning Slash as the actual mechanical lever.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling is already core in report[8], which is the right answer to Kingslayer's champion-only healing on a 12s cooldown.

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Sylas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Spin up fury on the wave — Sylas has only Chain Lash at 1 and no Kingslayer heal yet, so the walk-up trade is yours.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Abscond / Abduct's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your window: Bloodlust out-heals Kingslayer, and Spinning Slash at 12s is a second shorter than his Abscond at every rank.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sylas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Hijack is his spike, not yours: it steals Undying Rage, and at 80s against your 120s he gets the unkillable window back sooner than you do.

edits.before: Sylas favours L6 — Hijack steals your Undying Rage for a free unkillable window on his terms.
edits.after: Sylas favours L6 — Hijack steals Undying Rage, and at 80s it returns before your 120s does.

edits.before: This is Sylas's spike, not yours — he steals your Undying Rage with Hijack (R) and gains a free unkillable window, so don't force an even fight at 6; wait for his R cooldown before committing.
edits.after: This is Sylas's spike: Hijack (R) steals Undying Rage, and at 80s rank 1 against your 120s he gets the unkillable window back sooner than you do — so do not force an even fight at 6.

edits.before: Level 3-5 stays yours: bait Kingslayer (W), all-in when it's down, and your heal beats his poke-and-sustain pattern. He'll try to E away, so use W Mocking Shout to keep him in range while you swing.
edits.after: Level 3-5 stays yours: bait Kingslayer (W), all-in on its 12s, and Bloodlust beats his poke-and-sustain. He will Abscond away, but Spinning Slash is a second shorter at every rank — you get the last dash.

edits.before: Use E dash-stun mobility to disengage your all-in and reset
edits.after: Use Abscond (E) to dash out of your all-in and reset

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Abscond: 13s at rank 1 — Spinning Slash is 12s, exactly one second shorter at every rank, so you always get the last dash. - Kingslayer heals off you every 12s, so time Grievous Wounds to it. - Hijack: 80s against your 120s.

edits.before: Track Sylas's Abscond / Abduct: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. When it is down — Spin in, crit him down.
edits.after: Abscond has no stun — the recast pulls Sylas to you, not you to him. At 13s it is always a second longer than your E.

edits.before: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Abscond is a dash, not a stun; the recast drags him to you. Bait it, then commit on 13s.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Kingslayer heals him off you — land Grievous Wounds before it.

notes: Abscond / Abduct was called a 'dash + stun' in four fields; Riot's text has no stun and the recast pulls Sylas to the target, not the target to Sylas. The page also told players to 'wait out the long Hijack cooldown' — Hijack is 80/55/30 against Undying Rage's 120/100/80, so it is the shorter of the two ultimates and the advice was inverted. Whether Hijack can be cast on Tryndamere while Undying Rage is already active, or whether the stolen copy carries its own cooldown, is not in this data.
